claim: Soar-style episodic memory (automatic snapshot write, deliberate cue read, best-match, step next/previous, failure signal) lets an agent learn action models, evaluate decisions from past outcomes and do virtual sensing in toy domains.
agent_test: Implement S0 class record with automatic write and cue-based read; compare to no-record at equal tokens on repeated-task items.
audit_note: All listed sources (Nuxoll and Laird 2012, Derbinsky/Li/Laird 2012, Laird 2022) are from the Laird Soar group, so the demonstrated capabilities (action modelling, decision evaluation, virtual sensing) rest on one lab's own toy-domain demos; the findings themselves match the papers, with learning curves given only as graphs.

claim: Matching episodes by feature count alone gives little over random; bias by activation/recency or deliberately designed cues is needed. Retrieval with the wrong cue is the main failure.
agent_test: Ablate recency bias in record retrieval; measure hit rate of the useful past record.
audit_note: Minor: Nuxoll 2004 says unbiased matching gave only moderately-better-than-random scores and the activation-biased match performed significantly better; 'retrieval with the wrong cue is the main failure' is a synthesis (Nuxoll notes identical cues for every move, RMM calls retrieval the bottleneck), not a single quoted finding.

claim: Soar can learn WHEN and HOW to retrieve (cue choice, step-next) by RL, but convergence depends on the exploration schedule.
agent_test: Learn a retrieve/skip policy from reward at equal tokens; low priority, needs many trials.

claim: Soar RL only tunes operator choice among otherwise-undecided candidates; hard-coded safety knowledge stays in charge.
agent_test: Keep guardrails as veto; let learned preferences only break ties among operators.
audit_note: Minor: Laird 2022 (section 5) states this directly; the Soar manual RL chapter only says Q-values are numeric-indifferent preferences, and the second Laird listing is the same paper.

claim: Plain TD-style RL fails with hidden state; adding a short episodic history hash to specialise rules fixes it in a toy domain.
agent_test: Include a recent-history cue in the operator-preference record when outcomes vary on identical visible state.

claim: Episodic retrieval cost grows with agent lifespan; algorithmic indexing keeps it real time up to about 10^8 episodes, but cost depends on cue type and structure growth.
agent_test: Not binding for an LLM agent; cap record size and measure retrieval latency.

claim: Soar episodic memory has no generalisation, forgetting or consolidation; a separate semantic store holds context-free facts.
agent_test: Keep S0 records episodic and store distilled lessons separately; test lesson distillation vs raw replay.
audit_note: Minor: Nuxoll and Laird 2012 say memory consolidation, forgetting and generalisation are not included; Soar manual says epmem has no forgetting; Laird 2022 says no generalisation; all from one lab and some are version-specific.

claim: In LLM agents, written lessons from failed attempts (episodic buffer plus reflection) improve repeated-trial performance: Reflexion ALFWorld +22 points in 12 trials, HotPotQA +20, reflection adds 8 points over last-trajectory-only (N=100).
agent_test: Run retry with lesson record vs retry with raw last trajectory vs no memory at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: +22/+20 are Reflexion's abstract-level gains over strong baselines (ALFWorld 12 trials); +8 is Reflexion vs episodic-only on 100 HotPotQA questions with ground-truth context; ExpeL/ReasoningBank are related but do not restate these numbers.

claim: Memory without a trustworthy verifier can hurt: on HumanEval Rust (N=50 hardest) removing self-written tests dropped accuracy to 52%, below base 60%; omitting reflection returned to 60%; full Reflexion 68%.
agent_test: Gate any record write on a verifier outcome.

claim: LLM agents copy outputs of the most similar stored record (experience-following), so wrong stored records propagate and misaligned records mislead. Strict selection before writing and history-based deletion help; coarse evaluators remove the gain.
agent_test: Write-gating test: add-all vs verified-only vs verified plus deletion; measure error propagation over 100+ items.

claim: Structured memory stores often do not beat plain long context. Mem0 paper: full context 72.90 J (26,031 tokens) vs Mem0 66.88, Mem0g 68.44; independent test (Hu 2026): Mem0 21.1 and Zep 24.0 overall vs backbone GPT-4o-mini 42.3 and BM25 RAG 41.5; long-context GPT-5-mini 60.6.
agent_test: Compare S0 record vs stuffing full history at equal tokens; expect full history to win when it fits.
audit_note: Minor: the Hu comparison uses different benchmark/metrics from the Mem0 paper, and the Mem0 paper is a vendor paper; the numbers all match.

claim: Long-term chat memory is hard: LongMemEval shows about a 30% drop for long context (GPT-4o 0.870 to 0.606), commercial ChatGPT 0.5773 vs offline reading 0.9184; on LoCoMo the best base model (GPT-4-turbo, 4K context) reaches F1 32.4 and long-context or RAG variants about 38-41, vs human 87.9. Fact-augmented keys +9.4% recall, time-aware query expansion +6.8% to 11.3% recall.
agent_test: Use index design (fact keys, time) in record keys; test on a LongMemEval subset.
audit_note: LoCoMo F1 32.4 is the best of the limited-context base models (GPT-4-turbo, 4K); the same paper reports long-context GPT-3.5-16K at 37.8 and RAG GPT-3.5-16K up to about 41.4 overall, so 32.4 is not the best model overall. LongMemEval and key/time-expansion numbers check out.
claim_before_audit: Long-term chat memory is hard: LongMemEval about 30% drop for long context (GPT-4o 0.870 to 0.606), commercial ChatGPT 0.5773 vs offline reading 0.9184; LoCoMo best model F1 32.4 vs human 87.9. Fact-augmented keys +9.4% recall, time-aware query +11.3%.

claim: Self-managed paging of memory by the LLM lifts deep memory retrieval (GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%).
agent_test: Let the agent decide when to query its record; compare to always-retrieve.

claim: Believability of agents drops when memory, reflection or planning is ablated (TrueSkill 29.89 full vs 21.21 fully ablated, 100 raters).
agent_test: Subjective rating; not decision-relevant for accuracy tasks.

claim: RL applied to memory operations (add/update/delete) with outcome reward beats scripted memory managers on LoCoMo with 152 training pairs, but requires weight training.
agent_test: Out of scope (training); approximate with prompt-level add/update/delete rules verified on outcome.

claim: Soar-group LLM work: vetting LLM-proposed knowledge inside the architecture before storing it raises success (STARS 77.5/94.4/92.9 vs template 52.5/66.7/35.7).
agent_test: Verify candidate lessons by replay before committing to the class record.

claim: We found no published study that runs Soar episodic memory or Soar-RL against an LLM-agent memory on one benchmark; the Soar-to-LLM link in the sources read (CoALA, Pink et al. position paper, Wray/Kirk/Laird design patterns) is conceptual.
agent_test: An own experiment would be new.
audit_note: CoALA, Pink et al. and Wray/Kirk/Laird are indeed conceptual or position papers with no experiments, but none of them can establish that no study exists; the universal negative is unsupported by the listed sources.
claim_before_audit: No published study runs Soar episodic memory or Soar-RL against an LLM-agent memory on one benchmark; the Soar-to-LLM link is conceptual (CoALA, position papers).

claim: Distilled lessons beat raw earlier trajectories in context: ReasoningBank WebArena 48.8 vs raw-trajectory memory 42.1 vs none 40.5 (Gemini-2.5-flash); gains hold on three backbones and on SWE-Bench-Verified (+3.4 to +4.6). Not token-matched.
agent_test: Equal-token test: distilled class record vs raw prior solutions vs no record.

claim: Raw full-history appending can be worse than no memory (GPT-4o AIME 2024 20.0 baseline, 6.7 with full history, 40.0 with curated cheatsheet). Success-only workflow memory can fall below no memory on transfer (AWM 3.4 vs 10.3 on WebArena Multi, 29 tasks).
agent_test: Never default to dumping history; compare against curated record.

claim: Write gating works with a modest verifier if lessons are stored as abstractions: a 72.7%-accurate judge, and simulated 70-90% judges, gave similar gains; a hard execution signal lets memory help without labels; with no reliable signal memory can degrade.
agent_test: Gate record writes on a programmatic check; measure with a degraded verifier.
audit_note: Minor: ReasoningBank's simulated-judge result is read from a figure (flat across 70-90%, best at 100%) on one WebArena-Shopping subset with one judge model.

claim: Retrieval cue quality is a large lever: ALFWorld task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs random 42.5; LongMemEval RAG 63.6 vs oracle retrieval 90.2 and RMM 70.4. Cue with state plus proposed operator not tested in LLM agents.
agent_test: Ablate cue fields in the record read; report hit rate.
audit_note: Minor: ExpeL's task-similarity retrieval (59.0) vs random (42.5) is a single ALFWorld ablation; 63.6 is the best plain RAG (GTE) and 70.4 RMM, 90.2 oracle (Gemini-1.5-Flash); the not-tested-in-LLM-agents statement is an absence claim no source can confirm.

claim: LLMs do not explore reliably in context; one of 168 prompt/model configs worked, and it needed a code-computed per-option outcome summary. In-context operator preference from outcome counts therefore needs the counts computed outside the model.
agent_test: Keep per-operator success counts in the record; compare with fixed operator order.

claim: Memory benefit persists on a 2025 frontier model in agent tasks (GPT-5.1 AppWorld +11.6 average with ACE), but R1 and o1 gained little or inconsistently from a cheatsheet on reasoning tasks. Effect with extended thinking is untested directly.
agent_test: Run record on/off with thinking on and off.

claim: Rewriting the whole memory with an LLM collapses it (18,282 tokens to 122, accuracy 66.7 to 57.1, below 63.7 baseline); incremental deltas with counters avoid this.
agent_test: Edit the record by append and counter, never by full rewrite.
